severity_note: Public API (SCOTCH_meshBuild + SCOTCH_meshOrder, default strategy) on any element-weighted mesh large enough to be dissected; memory over-read plus wrong weights; meshes from files are unaffected (single shared load array).
evidence: mesh_induce_sepa.c:180 `if (orgmeshptr->velotax != NULL) {` ... :185 `&indmeshptr->velotax, (size_t) (orgsepanbr * sizeof (Gnum)), NULL); /* Element vertices assumed not weighted */` :230 `indvnloval  = orgmeshptr->velotax[orgvnodnum];` :347 `indmeshptr->vnlosum = (indmeshptr->velotax == NULL) ? orgsepanbr : indvnlosum;` ; hmesh_order_hx.c:106 `const Gnum * restrict const velotax = meshptr->m.velotax;` :130 `nvtax[vertnum]  = (velotax != NULL) ? velotax[vnodnum] : 1;` :168 same for halo nodes.

review_accuracy: Mechanism, locations and Fix line are right. The 8x8 reproducer cannot reach the code (81 nodes < the 120-node dissection threshold); the ASan 'heap-buffer-overflow' needs a guard page or a particular layout. It missed the second instance in hmeshOrderHxFill (same pattern, same inputs), which the Fix line as written would leave in place: with it alone, element-weighted meshes still read past the array in every HD/HF leaf ordering.
first_pass_critique: Status, reproducer and preferred option are right, and its remark on meshLoad sharing one array is correct. It missed hmesh_order_hx.c:130/168 (same defect, also reached by its own 30x30 test since the leaves use d{}), so its diff was incomplete. It proposed a regression test without noticing that a plain test cannot see the over-read: with vnlotab allocated right after velotab the pristine code reads the right loads by accident; the committed test places the element load array last and checks that unit element loads leave the ordering unchanged, which pristine violates.
